policy.title: Fed holds rates steady
policy.detail: The FOMC kept the federal funds target range at 3.75–4.00% in a 10–2 vote; Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point hike. Next decision is Dec 9.
policy.impact: No new upward push on borrowing costs from this meeting; mortgage rates still track inflation data and bond yields.

policy.title: New housing executive order signed
policy.detail: “Decreasing Housing Costs for the American People”: FHFA pilot to cancel mortgage insurance once equity is met at current value (future loans), makes the refi title-insurance waiver permanent, creates a manufactured-housing task force, and tells VA and USDA to lower their loan rates.
policy.impact: Mostly helps refis and FHA/VA/USDA borrowers; little near-term effect on Marin price points.

policy.title: Fannie & Freddie stay in conservatorship for now
policy.detail: Treasury Secretary Bessent said ownership changes are a next-year-or-later question and called mortgage rates the administration's North Star.
policy.impact: Removes a near-term rate-spike risk from a GSE release.

policy.title: FHFA weighs dropping 3-bureau credit pulls
policy.detail: Director Pulte said FHFA is studying one or two credit reports instead of three for Fannie/Freddie loans, with a decision on loan-level price adjustments (LLPAs) before year end.
policy.impact: Could trim closing costs; watch for LLPA changes affecting buyer pricing.

policy.title: Fed raises rates 0.25 pt
policy.detail: First hike since 2023, to 3.75–4.00%. September minutes showed most officials expected another hike by year end.
policy.impact: Main driver behind 7%+ mortgage rates and the 10-yr above 5%.

policy.title: FHFA lowers GSE affordable-housing goals
policy.detail: 2026–2028 goals for Fannie and Freddie were scaled back; Congress has not passed GSE reform.
policy.impact: Less required support for lower-income loans.

policy.title: Two housing executive orders
policy.detail: EO 14393 (Promoting Access to Mortgage Credit) loosened lending/capital rules for smaller lenders; EO 14394 (Removing Regulatory Barriers to Affordable Home Construction) targets permitting and energy-code costs.
policy.impact: Supply effects depend on local zoning, so slow to reach Marin.

policy.title: Institutional-investor order + $200B MBS buy
policy.detail: Order to stop large institutional investors buying single-family homes; Fannie/Freddie directed to buy $200B in mortgage-backed securities.
policy.impact: Investor limits still need Congress to codify; a Treasury rule for corporate buyers is expected in early 2027.
